messages:
Sahil (Sales): Hey product — inbound from MintLeaf for a pilot. They want us to onboard `mintleaf-llama3-ft` plus a q4_8 quantized runtime, EU-only (data residency), and the ability to pin to a specific model version. They're asking for high priority next sprint and an SLA ~99.9. Can product/eng confirm feasibility, rough effort, and launch criteria? cc @Marina (solutions) @Alex (PM)
Marina (Solutions): Thanks — can you share expected qps, average token lengths, and whether they need audit logs or on-prem/private deployment? :clipboard:
Sahil (Sales): Pilot is small: expected peak ~5 QPS, typical <500 tokens per call. They require PII redaction hooks and at-rest EU residency. Prefer canary rollout inside EU first, then expand. License is OSS but legal wants to review.
Alex (PM): High-level checklist we should validate: 1) compatibility test with q4_8 quantization 2) reserved capacity + geo-routing available 3) canary smoke tests in EU region 4) pin/versioning mechanics confirmed 5) SLA and legal signoff. Also need a rollback/fallback plan (eg fallback to fp16 variant if quant fails). Who owns each piece?
Jordan (Infra): Quick notes from infra/runtime perspective: our q4_8 pipeline is still marked "experimental" for many Llama3 forks — we'll need a full compile/opt pass and perf benchmarking for this specific model. Expect ~1 day per compile + one-day perf bench run. Capacity: 1 reserved node pool looks ok for 5 QPS pilot but we need routing rules for EU-only. Estimated infra implementation time: 2-3 weeks (excluding legal).
Emily (Catalog): For catalog entry we need: canonical model name, license text, weights URL + sha256, default variant to display, and a suggested quant profile tag (e.g., `q4_8-mintleaf`). Also include any eval prompts/testset they want us to run as part of quality gating.
onboard-bot: Intake created: model_id=mintleaf-llama3-ft, priority=high, region=eu, sla_request=99.9, intake_ticket=#INC-4897
Marina (Solutions): Tradeoffs to call out to customer: if `q4_8` path fails quality/regression checks we can fall back to fp16 which increases cost and latency. Do they accept that tradeoff? Also confirm whether audit logs + long-term retention are required (affects storage/cost).
Sahil (Sales): They confirmed via email they accept fallback to fp16 for the pilot. They provided the weights URL and a permissive OSS license. They prefer pinning to `v1.2.0` as the canonical launch version. I'll attach links to the ticket.
Alex (PM): OK, proposed owners & timeline: Product (me) — finalize launch criteria, customer comms; Eng-runtime (Jordan) — compatibility + perf; Infra (Jordan) — reserved pool + geo-routing; Catalog (Emily) — metadata + staging entry; Solutions (Marina) — SLA/legal coordination. Proposed target: canary in EU in ~3 weeks. If any owner believes this is optimistic, flag now.
Jordan (Infra): 3 weeks is tight given compile + infra + e2e. Realistic target is 4 weeks for a clean canary with perf baselines and rollback gating. If we parallelize compile and infra work it's doable but requires dedicated infra eng time this sprint.
Alex (PM): Thanks — bumping to 4 weeks. I'll add this as a high-priority customer-driven item in the backlog and create sub-tasks. Marina — can you get SLA & legal review by EOW so we don't block implementation?
Marina (Solutions): On it. I'll ping legal and attach the license + data residency note to #INC-4897.
Sahil (Sales): Great — I'll update the customer with the 4-week target and explain the fallback behavior. Also asking them to provide a small eval set for our quality checks.
Emily (Catalog): I'll draft the staging catalog entry template and request the metadata fields via the ticket. Tagging `catalog-team` for visibility.
Alex (PM): Nice. Action items captured: 1) Sahil — attach weights + eval set to INC-4897 (customer) 2) Marina — legal/SLA by EOW 3) Jordan — compatibility + infra plan and ETA 4) Emily — catalog staging entry 5) Alex — add to sprint backlog. Will follow up with a short runbook for the canary.
Jordan (Infra): Confirming resource request: need one infra engineer for 2 sprints to hit the 4-week date. Please mark as "requires infra support" on the ticket.
Sahil (Sales): Marked. Thanks all.
Marina (Solutions): I'll update the intake with the legal timeline and the customer's acceptance of fallback.
Alex (PM): Closing loop here — I'll create the backlog item now and link to INC-4897. We'll reconvene in the product sync tomorrow if any blockers appear. Thanks everyone :+1:
